hints.content: The arrow points to all values greater than $4$.
And the point at $4$ is *not* filled in.
So, the inequality represents everything strictly **greater than $4$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**



[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at 4. A line running to the right starts at 4 and continues.

choices.clue:
The graph of $x < 4$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at 4. A line running to the left starts at 4 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/3bcf9457a8ccfcc572a451a55eb860060c5ad671)

The graph of $x \leq 4$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A closed point is plotted at 4. A line running to the left starts at 4 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/61058b8f3c7179db2d74251814d9a735a8bb624c)

The graph of $x \geq 4$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A closed point is plotted at 4. A line running to the right starts at 4 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/fa056f28698c3094905d4d5d92700c3d4fa92268)
